proposed.explanation: Both appear in classical and modern contexts. Both can use identical or equivalent elements. Both can be formal depending on context. Critical distinction: bilateral symmetry = about an AXIS (forms mirror across a line); radial symmetry = around a POINT (forms balance in all directions). A building's front elevation showing mirrored wings = bilateral. A rotunda or central courtyard with radiating elements = radial. A rotunda or central courtyard with radiating elements = radial.
